subtitle: AI-first product flows, complex workflow tools and prototypes that reach the product

bio.short: I design software for people trying to get their work done, and I do that work hands-on. At Bibel TV, I redesigned an AI feature and weekly starts rose 153% on iOS and 85% on Android. At Ninox, I designed AI onboarding where the generated database stays visible and editable. At ChurchDesk, a multi-party booking workflow took an estimated 70% less coordination and shipped to the full customer base.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV, I redesigned the AI Bible-passage feature end to end. Weekly starts rose from 205 to 518 on iOS and from 655 to 1,213 on Android, each measured in GA4 over four full weeks before and after its own release. I also prototype in working code against production APIs, directing and reviewing AI coding agents. 64% of the code behind the redesigned Home and detail views of the Android app (release 6.0, in beta) comes verbatim from my prototype.

At Ninox, a no-code platform where customers digitize processes such as construction site inspections, I owned the design system and defined its easing curves and small animations. Working as a freelancer in summer 2025, I came back to design prompt-to-database AI onboarding. People rarely describe their work in full, so the first schema is often slightly wrong. I put the generated database in the real editor beside chat, where people can see it and change it directly.

At ChurchDesk, I owned product management for the main platform and led product design. Starting from a launch customer's workshop output, with two months until development release, I turned a multi-party funeral-booking process into a capability inside the existing calendar and form builder. Coordination time fell by an estimated 70%, booking acceptance reached 90%, and the capability shipped to the full customer base.

context.company: ToolTime builds cloud software with automation and intelligence for tradespeople and craft businesses.
context.role: A hands-on senior design owner for one product area in a cross-functional squad, leading AI-first experiences for a defined 16-month engagement.
context.emphasis: Lead with the measured AI feature and editable AI output, then the operational workflow at ChurchDesk and prototypes that engineering builds from.
